title: Permutation-driven AB harness with early-revert policy for model rollouts
creator: Sofia Park
description: Build an AB testing harness that uses permutation-based sequential checks to enable statistically robust canary rollouts with automated early-revert when signal indicates regression.
background: Current model rollout tooling supports fixed-sample A/B splits and threshold-based rollbacks. We need a more robust statistical engine for short-lived canaries and per-request heterogeneity where parametric tests underperform. Permutation testing reduces distributional assumptions and pairs well with sequential monitoring on streaming traffic.
proposal: Implement a new experiment controller that: 1) performs stratified permutation tests on rolling windows of requests for primary KPIs; 2) supports per-request matching (control/model) to reduce variance; 3) provides configurable early-revert policies (alpha spending, minimum sample, hysteresis); 4) integrates with runtime routing to dynamically adjust traffic share and shadowing; 5) surfaces decision insights to Console with visualized p-value trajectories and explained drivers. The controller will run in the control plane and call a stats worker service for heavy computations.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can instantiate AB experiments with permutation sequential checks
System triggers automated rollback when configured thresholds and spending functions are exceeded
Console shows live p-value curve, sample counts, and top contributing covariate drift signals
Routing layer honors dynamic traffic adjustments within 5s of controller decision
Unit and e2e tests for at least three scenarios: no-diff, improvement, regression
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (sprint 1-2): stats worker + API + minimal console endpoints behind feature flag
Phase 2 (sprint 3): integrate with routing runtime and shadow traffic path
Phase 3 (sprint 4): production smoke with internal models, monitor 2 weeks
Phase 4: open to customers as opt-in with guardrails and docs
test_plan: Simulated traffic replay using historical 6 month request logs with injected signal scenarios
Chaos tests: delayed metric visibility and partial worker failures
Canary on internal staging fleet at 0.5% traffic for 48h
A/B edge cases: high-cardinality cohorts (user locale, device), and bursty traffic
notes: Use stratified block-permutation for small sample cohorts
Start with primary metrics that are near-ratio stable; avoid rare-event metrics initially
Consider approximate permutation via Monte Carlo sampling to bound compute cost
Add audit log entries for every automated rollback decision
